headline: The US OK'd 500 Patriots for Ukraine. Allies pay the bill.
summary: The State Department approved on Friday selling Ukraine 500 Patriot interceptors for $2.1bn. Canada, Germany, Norway and an EU loan cover all of it, no US money. Zelensky says Ukraine waited almost a month for the sign-off and is running low as Russia hits power plants before winter. They're new builds, and the US makes about 600 a year.

cover_question.q: Why is the US short on them?

cover_answer: It fired its own at Iran. It builds about 600 a year.
table_question: If a friend needs help and someone else pays, is it still your gift?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Ukraine is a faraway country in a war. Rockets fly at its cities. A Patriot is a rocket that goes up and knocks the other one down before it lands, like a goalkeeper blocking a shot. America said yes to selling Ukraine 500, and its friends in Europe and Canada are paying. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: A goalkeeper is a thing a six-year-old has seen. The missile only blocks, which is the one fact that matters at this age.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, and a rocket is frightening, so the script makes it a goalkeeper: it only blocks. Cantor found fear at this age comes from the picture, not the politics, and here the picture is a save. Expect "Could a rocket come here?" Say no, it is far away, and these only stop rockets.

8-12.script: Russia fires ballistic missiles at Ukraine's power plants, and only the Patriot reliably stops them. Ukraine was nearly out and waited almost a month for the US to sign off. Friday it did: 500 missiles, $2.1bn, paid by Canada, Germany, Norway and an EU loan. Built to order, about 600 a year.
8-12.why: Kids this age get a queue: few made, many needed. The waiting is the part they'll want explained.
8-12.why_long: At this age a child is building chains of cause and effect, so the script hands them one: Russia fires, only Patriots stop it, Ukraine ran low, the US signed, the factory makes 600 a year. The last link is the lesson: a yes is not a delivery. Expect "Why did it take a month?" Say Zelensky blames the US, and the article does not say why.

13-17.script: Does it count as helping if someone else pays? The US approved 500 Patriots for Ukraine days after Trump said Ukraine needs a new leader, and not a US dollar is in it. They're new builds in a world short of them, since the US used its own against Iran. Who gets the next 600 off the line?
13-17.why: Teenagers can hold the sale and the insult side by side. Let them say which one tells them more about the policy.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can reason about what is not in front of them, so the script hands them the gap between a signature and a delivery and asks who is next in a queue. It holds two facts: the sale went through, and the president just told Ukraine to change leaders. Expect "So is the US helping or not?" Say both, and ask what they would watch.

5-7.a: No. Ukraine is across an ocean, and these rockets only stop other rockets.

8-12.a: Patriots are the only weapon that stops Russia's ballistic missiles.

8-12.q: Why did it take a month?
8-12.a: Zelensky says the US sat on it. The article doesn't say why.

13-17.q: Why is the US short on them?
13-17.a: It used its own stock against Iran. It builds about 600 a year.

13-17.q: Didn't Trump just turn on Zelensky?
13-17.a: He said days ago it's time for a new leader. The sale went through anyway.
